# Experiments

Requirements extracted from [`SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md). This view is for focused reading and review; the spec text is normative.

## ER

- **ER-1** — **Core comparison.** Learned, classical and ER-9 control systems, full test split, every SNR in `params.channel.test_snr_grid_db`, at `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` — which resolves to `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio`, because a crossover claimed from a one-seed sweep figure while the full-strength intervals sit at a different budget would rest the project's most contested result on its weakest evidence (AM-20) — repeated over the seed cells defined by `params.evaluation.seed_pairing` — `params.evaluation.train_seeds` **zipped with** `params.evaluation.channel_seeds`, giving three cells, not their nine-cell cross product — reported with `params.evaluation.ci` intervals, measuring `params.project.primary_metric`. Rationale: the conjunction was ambiguous and the two readings differ threefold in evaluation cost; §16's decode-throughput estimate was written against three cells, and a third channel realisation of an already-frozen model buys far less than a third training run does (AM-17). Models are trained per DEC-11. Hypotheses are decided by §2 via ER-10. *(verify: results CSV + accuracy-vs-SNR figure, with exactly one row group per seed cell)*
- **ER-2** — **SNR mismatch.** Train once at `params.channel.train_snr_db_fixed`, evaluate across the whole test grid, and report the degradation profile of both systems to evidence the cliff-versus-graceful contrast (H2). An **SNR-randomised learned variant** trained over `params.channel.train_snr_db_set` MUST also be reported, at one entry in `params.evaluation.train_seeds` and at `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` — one training run. Rationale: BR-15 discloses that the baseline re-tunes at every SNR while the learned model is frozen, and that asymmetry favours the baseline at *both* ends of the grid, including inside H1's region where the baseline may drop to BPSK for roughly 3 dB of extra reach. This was previously OPT-4, non-blocking and therefore unlikely to be run; the objection it answers — "your learned system was not allowed to adapt and the baseline was" — is one an examiner will raise, and `params.channel.train_snr_db_set` already existed in this file serving nothing else (AM-45). *(verify: results CSV + figure, with the fixed-SNR and SNR-randomised learned curves present as distinct `system` values)*
- **ER-3** — **Operating-point selection and bandwidth sweep.** Before the headline run, sweep every entry in `params.bandwidth.ratios` **with the classical system only**, on the **full validation split** at one seed, and select **two** operating points at G-8 by this preregistered, **learned-blind** rule applied at two thresholds: *the smallest ratio at which the classical system's high-SNR ceiling comes within `t` percentage points of its clean-image accuracy*, evaluated at `t` = `params.bandwidth.efficiency_ratio_threshold_pp` to give `params.bandwidth.efficiency_ratio`, and at `t` = `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio_threshold_pp` to give `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio`. Both are lookups against the same classical sweep table, so the second threshold costs nothing to evaluate, and the two MAY select the same ratio — in which case there is one operating point and `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` resolves to it unchanged. **If no ratio satisfies the crossover threshold while some ratio satisfies the efficiency threshold**, `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio` resolves to the largest ratio in `params.bandwidth.ratios`, `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` resolves to `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio_unsatisfiable_fallback` instead, and the absence of a 2 pp ratio is reported as a first-class finding under DEC-16's fallback. This is preregistered here rather than settled at G-8 because G-8 holds the classical sweep table in hand, and 2 pp is a demanding bar for a lossy codec scored by a clean-trained classifier — the asymmetric failure is the likely one, and G-8's existing fallback covers only the symmetric case where the rule fails at every threshold (AM-41). Rationale for two: the looser threshold locates the **efficiency point**, the tightest budget at which the baseline is still healthy, which is where the bandwidth claim lives; but "within 5 points of clean" admits a classical ceiling around 0.83 while the learned ceiling is estimated at 0.85–0.87, so that threshold can select a ratio at which no crossover exists at all. The tighter threshold locates the **crossover point**, the smallest budget at which the classical ceiling can actually overtake the learned one. Reporting both shows the trade-off as a function of budget rather than asserting it at a point (AM-20). The rule inspects only the classical system at either threshold, so it cannot be accused of selecting for the hypothesis; it places the comparison where the baseline is healthy rather than where it is starved, and tightening a threshold hands the baseline *more* budget, which DEC-16's governing rule expressly permits. Because BR-4 now adapts modulation as well (DEC-16), the classical ceiling rises faster with SNR than it would under a fixed modulation, so the rule is expected to select a *smaller* ratio than it otherwise would — the crossover is bought with better use of the budget rather than with more budget. The sweep also reports `params.bandwidth.low_ratio_operating_point` as the bandwidth-starved regime where dominance rather than crossover is expected. That point is resolved at G-8 by `params.bandwidth.low_ratio_rule` rather than read as a fixed value: it was hard-coded at `r_1_12` while `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` is selected, so if the rule selects a smaller ratio than `r_1_12` the "starved" point sits *above* the operating point and the regime it names does not exist — leaving §2's expectation of low-ratio dominance with no experiment behind it (AM-41). For the same reason the ladder MUST NOT be allowed to saturate at its bottom: per `params.bandwidth.ladder_bottom_saturation_rule`, if the rule selects the smallest ratio in `params.bandwidth.ratios` the ladder MUST be extended downward and the classical-only sweep re-run before the selection is recorded. `r_1_48` was added for this reason and is free architecturally — it is exactly one complex channel at the 4x-downsampled grid on all three datasets, where `r_1_32` would need 1.5 and is therefore not usable. Because the rule is learned-blind, learned systems MUST be trained at `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio`, `params.bandwidth.efficiency_ratio` and `params.bandwidth.low_ratio_operating_point` **only** — at most three ratios, and two if the thresholds coincide — nothing in §2 needs a learned model at every ratio, and training five would spend roughly nine runs to inform a decision that cannot see them (AM-12). The sweep uses the full validation split rather than `params.evaluation.test_subset_size`: that parameter sizes a subset of the *test* split under ER-6, and at 2000 it exceeds the `val_images` count of every dataset in `params.datasets`, so the requirement as previously written could not be executed at all (AM-14). *(verify: results CSV + figure, an archived record of the rule's evaluation at every ratio, and an assertion that no learned-system row exists at a ratio outside the ratios named here — previously "the two named here", which contradicted this requirement's own body naming three, a stale clause AM-20 left behind (AM-26))*
- **ER-4** — **Task-training ablation.** The semantic reconstruction head MUST also be scored through the frozen `params.reference_classifier` (BR-8), separating gain attributable to joint coding from gain attributable to a task-trained classifier. Reported as a distinct `system` value. *(verify: results CSV containing the ablation rows)*
- **ER-5** — Every experiment MUST emit rows matching `params.artifacts.csv_schema` exactly — same columns, same order — alongside the per-image file required by SR-18. *(verify: schema validation script over all result CSVs)*
- **ER-6** — Evaluation on `params.evaluation.test_subset_size` images is permitted for sweeps only; `params.evaluation.full_test_split_required_for` MUST use the full split, and the `test_subset` column MUST record which was used. *(verify: schema test asserting the flag)*
- **ER-7** — Every number appearing in the thesis MUST be traceable to a `run_id` and `git_commit` in a committed CSV. *(verify: audit script resolving each reported figure to its rows)*
- **ER-8** — If a hypothesis in §2 is unsupported, the negative result MUST be reported with the same rigour as a positive one, together with the diagnostic evidence. Weakening the baseline to manufacture support is prohibited. *(verify: review against BR-4 sweep artifacts and BR-11 overhead tables)*
- **ER-9** — **Task-aware digital control.** A third system MUST be built and evaluated at matched `k`, sharing every element in `params.digital_semantic_control.shared_with_learned` with the learned JSCC system and differing from it **only** in `params.digital_semantic_control.differs_only_in`: features taken at `params.digital_semantic_control.transmit_layer` are quantised per `params.digital_semantic_control.quantiser` at a width selected from `params.digital_semantic_control.quantiser_bits_grid` on the validation split (DEC-12), entropy-coded per `params.digital_semantic_control.entropy_coder`, and carried over the same `params.baseline.channel_code` chain as the classical baseline with its transport configuration tuned per `params.digital_semantic_control.transport_tuning`. It MUST be scored by `params.digital_semantic_control.scored_by` — a task head architecturally identical to the learned system's — **not** by the frozen `params.reference_classifier`, which consumes images and cannot read a feature stream (AM-5). **The transmitted dimension is ER-9's own and is selected, not inherited (AM-55).** `params.digital_semantic_control.transmit_dim_grid`, in `params.digital_semantic_control.transmit_dim_units`, is chosen jointly with the quantiser width on the validation split per `params.digital_semantic_control.width_selection`, realised per `params.digital_semantic_control.transmit_dim_realised_by`, and searched per `params.digital_semantic_control.selection_search` — two-stage, with `params.digital_semantic_control.selection_search_is_cross_product` false, so W9's training count stays bounded. Matched `k` then fixes the budget: transmitted dimension × quantiser width, after entropy coding and including container overhead, MUST fit the same `params.baseline.budget_rule` payload the classical baseline receives. **This replaces a specification that was arithmetically infeasible at every operating point but one.** `transmit_feature_dim` was previously shared with the learned system, pinning the dimension at 2k real values while the digital budget supplies only `Q_m × R / 2` bits per value — 1.67 at 16-QAM rate 5/6, 0.5 at QPSK rate 1/2, and 0.167 at BPSK rate 1/3, against a 2-bit floor in `params.digital_semantic_control.quantiser_bits_grid`. Every configuration except 16-QAM at rate 5/6 was therefore impossible, and that one decodes only above roughly 11 dB — outside H1's region entirely — so ER-9 would have been pinned at outage and scored at chance across exactly the range H4 is tested in, making the control unfalsifiable and H4 trivially easy to support. That is the AM-15 failure class and the direction ER-8 forbids. Choosing how many values to send against how precisely to send each one **is** the digital channel interface — an analog system makes no such choice — so this remains a difference in `params.digital_semantic_control.differs_only_in` rather than an addition to it, and `params.digital_semantic_control.channel_interface_comprises` names its three components. Feasibility is now verified rather than assumed: at the tightest live configuration, STL-10 at the low ratio with BPSK rate 1/3 and 94 payload bytes, seven (dimension, width) pairs fit. Rationale: without a control that is task-aware *and* digital, the learned-versus-classical gap conflates task-aware representation with joint coding and §1 claim 2 cannot be attributed (H4); and unless the control shares the learned system's front end, a measured difference could equally be architecture, capacity or training objective rather than the channel interface. This is the primary novelty claim of DEC-13. **The entropy table is not charged per image**, per `params.digital_semantic_control.entropy_table_bytes_counted`: the model is fitted offline on the training split and installs at both endpoints alongside the network weights, exactly like the quantiser scales, the JPEG 2000 coding rules and the LDPC matrices, none of which are charged either. Charging it would weaken the control on every image and make H4 easier to support, which is the wrong direction to be wrong in. Only genuinely per-message metadata counts — stream length, any image-adaptive scale, and framing (AM-55). *(verify: results CSV rows under a distinct `system` value at the same k as ER-1, with the selected `quantiser_bits` and transmitted dimension recorded per row, plus an architecture-diff artifact showing that only `params.digital_semantic_control.differs_only_in` separates the two systems)*
- **ER-10** — **Paired inference.** The §2 hypotheses MUST be decided on **paired per-image outcomes** (SR-18), not on the overlap of two independent intervals: `params.evaluation.paired_test` for the point decision and `params.evaluation.ci` with `params.evaluation.bootstrap_resamples` for the interval on the accuracy *difference*, with the image-level bootstrap nested inside the seed hierarchy. Each seed cell is a **compound replicate** per `params.evaluation.seed_cell_interpretation`, and no claim is made that `params.evaluation.train_seeds` and `params.evaluation.channel_seeds` contribute as *separate* variance components. This requirement previously promised exactly that, which AM-17 made unachievable in the same round it was written: `params.evaluation.seed_pairing` zips the seeds into (0,0), (1,1), (2,2), so training luck and channel luck move together in every cell and no analysis can attribute a difference to one rather than the other. Three diagonal cells cannot separate two sources — the honest statement is that each cell is one combined replicate, and the per-seed curves below are what show the spread. Crossing the seeds into nine cells would restore the decomposition at roughly three times ER-1's evaluation cost, and was rejected because two degrees of freedom could not support the claim even then (AM-31). Rationale: both systems see identical images and noise draws, so a paired test is both the natural and the far more powerful analysis — a three-seed Student-t interval has two degrees of freedom and would demand roughly a five-point gap to clear non-overlap. Three further rules make the seed hierarchy honest, since `params.evaluation.bootstrap_resamples` resamples images and cannot manufacture training-run evidence that three seeds do not contain (AM-11): the **classical arm has no training-seed dimension** — it is never trained — so the training-seed variance component belongs to the learned arm alone and a classical result MUST NOT be replicated across seed cells and counted as independent baseline runs; `params.evaluation.paired_test` MUST be computed **within** a seed cell and never pooled across cells, which would treat repeated measurements of the same images as independent; and each seed's accuracy-vs-SNR curve MUST be reported separately alongside the between-seed range, so the reader sees training-run spread rather than inferring it from an interval that mostly reflects image count. ER-10 also computes `params.evaluation.h1_effect_size` and `params.evaluation.gap_trend_test` for §2's H1 and H3. Two further computations are required. **H1's run rule MUST be calibrated, not merely argued**: `params.evaluation.h1_run_calibration` over `params.evaluation.h1_run_permutation_resamples` resamples gives the null distribution of the longest run of positive intervals by sign-flipping whole per-image trajectories, which preserves the across-SNR correlation that makes the analytic argument in §2 a model assumption rather than a bound. The per-image outcomes SR-18 already requires are exactly the input this needs, so it is a few dozen lines beside a bootstrap that already runs (AM-32). **H3's slope MUST be bootstrapped over `params.evaluation.gap_trend_bootstrap_unit`** — per-image, per-seed trajectories — rather than over 18 aggregated SNR points, which are strongly correlated through shared images and shared models and would give an interval far too narrow (AM-39). *(verify: inference script reproducing every reported interval from the per-image files, with a unit test on synthetic data of known effect size, a test that no pooled-across-seeds McNemar statistic is emitted, and an archived permutation null distribution for the run statistic)*
- **ER-11** — **Bandwidth versus accuracy.** The learned system MUST be evaluated at **every** ratio DEC-11 trains it at — not `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` alone — across `params.channel.test_snr_grid_db`, at sweep strength per ER-6 and one entry in `params.evaluation.train_seeds`, with the classical curve at the same ratio, and reported as the bandwidth-versus-accuracy figure. Rationale: this closes the defect AM-12 fixed once and AM-20 reopened at reduced scale. DEC-11 trains up to three ratios, but ER-1 runs at the headline ratio alone, ER-2 names no ratio and ER-4 is an ablation of existing rows — so the `params.bandwidth.efficiency_ratio` and `params.bandwidth.low_ratio_operating_point` models were trained and then consumed by no requirement, no figure and no hypothesis. It matters beyond waste: DEC-16's last-resort fallback reports learned dominance across the whole grid, and the low-ratio regime is where that claim is strongest, so the evidence for it MUST already be a required output rather than something improvised at W12. At `params.evaluation.test_subset_size` and one seed this costs a few percent of ER-1 (AM-42). *(verify: results CSV rows at every trained ratio for both systems, plus the committed figure)*
- **ER-12** — **Label-transmission upper bound.** A reference curve MUST be reported in which the transmitter runs the task head locally and transmits only the predicted label over the same `params.baseline.channel_code` chain at matched `k`, reusing ER-9's encoder trunk, at one entry in `params.evaluation.train_seeds` and at `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio`. It MUST be labelled an **upper bound, not a matched comparator**, and MUST NOT appear in any §2 hypothesis. Rationale: for ten-class classification the complete task output is four bits, so an examiner can ask why the transmitter runs a neural encoder and sends thousands of symbols rather than attaching the head locally and protecting four bits heavily. §1 acknowledges that a digital transmitter could send "logits or labels" but ER-9 only builds the feature end of that spectrum, leaving the sharpest conceptual objection to the project unanswered by any experiment. The answer is the fixed-split premise §1 now states — the partition is imposed, the receiver owns the task head — and this curve makes the bound explicit rather than leaving it to be raised at a viva. It is nearly free, reusing a trained trunk (AM-40). *(verify: results CSV row under a distinct `system` value, and a caption stating the fixed-split premise and that the bound assumes a transmitter that already knows the answer)*
